ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A simple harmonic transverse wave, as shown in the figure, where the solid line represents the waveform at a certain moment, and the dashed line represents the waveform after 0.2 seconds.

1. Assuming the wave propagates to the left, find the possible distance it travels.
2. If this wave propagates to the right, find its maximum period.
3. Assuming the wave speed is $35\mathrm{m/s}$, determine the direction of wave propagation.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the horizontal axis is x/m, and the vertical axis is y. The black solid line represents the waveform at a certain moment, and the blue dashed line represents the waveform after 0.2 s. Observing adjacent wave crests of the same line type, the solid-line wave crests are approximately at x=0 and x=4, and the dashed-line wave crests are approximately at x=1 and x=5, so the wavelength λ=4 m. Compared with the dashed-line waveform, the solid-line waveform can equivalently be regarded as translated 1 m to the right, or 3 m to the left; because the waveform has periodicity, an integer number of wavelengths can also be added. Reasoning: 1. If the wave propagates to the left, one can take the solid-line wave crest x=0 moving after 0.2 s to the dashed-line in-phase wave crest x=-3, or the solid-line wave crest x=4 moving to the dashed-line in-phase wave crest x=1, so the minimum leftward moving distance is 3 m. Considering periodicity, the possible propagation distance is d=3+4n m, n=0,1,2,.... 2. If the wave propagates to the right, the minimum compatible displacement is that the solid-line wave crest x=0 moves to the dashed-line wave crest x=1, namely d=1+4n m. The phase advance after 0.2 s is d/λ=(1+4n)/4=n+1/4 periods, therefore 0.2/T=n+1/4, T=0.2/(n+1/4). When the period is maximum, n=0, so Tmax=0.2/(1/4)=0.8 s. 3. If the wave speed v=35 m/s, the propagation distance within 0.2 s is d=vt=35×0.2=7 m. 7=4×1+3, which conforms to the leftward propagation distance 3+4n m; while the rightward propagation distance should be 1+4n m, which does not include 7 m. Therefore the wave propagates to the left.
